messages.content: Return only JSON with keys choice,rationale,firstPatch,acceptance. We now have a tested long-lived NDJSON stdin/stdout inference broker with durable journal, restart dedupe, bounded queue, settlement-order output, graceful drain, provider price/capability routing, schema verification, and no network listener authority. Colonies still need an easy way to contract it without each manually launching a process. Choose the smallest next carrier from systemd-user-socket, unix-domain-socket-supervisor, ActivityStreams-adapter, filesystem-inbox-watcher, or other. Preserve the broker as the sole scheduler and do not create a global work pool. Specify an implementable first patch and 3 concise acceptance conditions.

completion.text: {"choice":"systemd-user-socket","rationale":"systemd-user-socket with Accept=no is the least new code: the OS binds the socket and activates the broker on first connect, colonies need only connect() to a well-known path, and the broker detects LISTEN_FDS to enter an accept loop that feeds the existing queue. No supervisor process, no polling, no protocol change. The broker remains the sole scheduler; the accept loop is a thin seam over the existing queue, not a new work pool.","firstPatch":"Add --socket-activate flag: when LISTEN_FDS=1 is set, call accept() on fd 3 in a loop; spawn one read-goroutine per accepted connection that pipes NDJSON lines into the existing bounded queue and writes settlement-order responses back on that connection fd. Ship inference-broker.socket (ListenStream=%t/inference-broker.sock, Accept=no) and inference-broker.service (ExecStart=broker --socket-activate, Type=simple) as ~/.config/systemd/user/ units. Zero changes to queue, journal, router, or dedupe logic.","acceptance":["systemctl --user start inference-broker.socket succeeds and a colony can write NDJSON to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/inference-broker.sock without manually launching the broker process.","Two concurrent colony connections each receive correctly routed, settlement-ordered responses with no line interleaving, and the journal records both request sets with deduplication intact.","systemctl --user stop inference-broker.service triggers graceful drain; all in-flight responses are written before the socket closes, and a subsequent colony connect auto-restarts the broker via socket activation."]}

structured_output.rationale: systemd-user-socket with Accept=no is the least new code: the OS binds the socket and activates the broker on first connect, colonies need only connect() to a well-known path, and the broker detects LISTEN_FDS to enter an accept loop that feeds the existing queue. No supervisor process, no polling, no protocol change. The broker remains the sole scheduler; the accept loop is a thin seam over the existing queue, not a new work pool.
structured_output.firstPatch: Add --socket-activate flag: when LISTEN_FDS=1 is set, call accept() on fd 3 in a loop; spawn one read-goroutine per accepted connection that pipes NDJSON lines into the existing bounded queue and writes settlement-order responses back on that connection fd. Ship inference-broker.socket (ListenStream=%t/inference-broker.sock, Accept=no) and inference-broker.service (ExecStart=broker --socket-activate, Type=simple) as ~/.config/systemd/user/ units. Zero changes to queue, journal, router, or dedupe logic.
acceptance: systemctl --user start inference-broker.socket succeeds and a colony can write NDJSON to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/inference-broker.sock without manually launching the broker process.
Two concurrent colony connections each receive correctly routed, settlement-ordered responses with no line interleaving, and the journal records both request sets with deduplication intact.

systemctl --user stop inference-broker.service triggers graceful drain; all in-flight responses are written before the socket closes, and a subsequent colony connect auto-restarts the broker via socket activation.
